supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records show approximately five-minute CONNECT attempts to update.chartmate-imaging.net:443 at 13:38:00, 13:43:20, 13:47:44, 13:52:37, 13:58:16, 14:03:02 and 14:08:00 UTC.

Endpoint and connection records attribute these proxy connections to PID 3416, C:\Users\ben.carter\AppData\Local\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe. It launched under ben.carter from explorer.exe at 13:37:57 UTC with --background.

The observed executable location and destination differ from the supplied approved ChartMate baseline: the executable runs from the user's AppData directory rather than C:\Program Files\ChartMate, and the destination ends in .net rather than the approved .com. These discrepancies make benign updater attribution unsafe, but do not alone establish maliciousness.

Five CONNECT requests established tunnels, each recording 5,397 client-to-server bytes and 31,383 server-to-client bytes. The other two attempts received proxy authentication-required (407) and gateway-error (502) responses; they should not be counted as successful outbound HTTPS tunnels.

A Sysmon file-creation event attributes creation of the executable's own pathname to PID 3416 shortly after its first recorded tunnel. This merits examination, but the event does not establish what bytes were written or whether this was malicious modification.
The process terminated at 14:08:34 UTC, after its final recorded periodic connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: The successful proxy records contain CONNECT tunnel metadata, not decrypted application requests or responses; their byte counts do not reveal commands, transferred files or payload contents (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
The process-creation and file-creation records do not supply executable hashes, signature verification or file contents needed to authenticate this updater (T015-00108, T015-00109, T015-00114).
The supplied periodic sequence is documented from 13:38 through 14:08 UTC, rather than establishing connections throughout the alert's entire stated 13:30–14:10 interval (T015-00110, T015-00281).
claims_not_established: Whether the AppData executable is an authentic alternate ChartMate installation or an impersonating program (T015-00108, T015-00109).
Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is vendor-controlled or malicious; its resemblance to the approved .com destination is not proof of either (T015-00110).
Whether the periodic tunnels carried update checks, command-and-control traffic or exfiltration (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
Whether the file-creation event represents legitimate updating, replacement or another operation (T015-00114).
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve the AppData cmupdate.exe and obtain its hash, verified digital signature, version metadata and provenance; compare it with a trusted ChartMate package.
Confirm with the software owner or vendor whether this AppData installation path and the .net update hostname are legitimate and authorized.
Obtain available proxy-side DNS, upstream connection and TLS certificate information for the .net destination, plus decrypted transaction content if already retained.
Collect installation history and surrounding file telemetry to explain the executable's launch and the file-creation event at its own pathname.
unrelated_findings: Separate software-inventory review: ZoomUpdate.exe executed as SYSTEM, ZSAService.exe started as SYSTEM, and a separate tunnel used a Duo Device Health user-agent. These products are not identified in the supplied approved-software list; these observations do not establish maliciousness or decide the periodic-connection alert (T015-00062, T015-00120, T015-00306).

Separate SMB review: FILE-HD-01 recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON from WS-BCARTER-01 at 13:54:48 UTC. The accompanying connection records do not identify accessed resources or link this session to the alerted updater process (T015-00253, T015-00254, T015-00257).
